title: AWS CloudTrail: who did what, when

kcs.statement: AWS CloudTrail records API calls and account activity made through the console, CLI, SDKs or other AWS services: who made the call, what it was, when, and from which IP address. This record is used for auditing and investigations.
CloudTrail event history shows the last 90 days of management events at no charge. Keeping logs longer requires a trail that delivers log files to an S3 bucket.
CloudTrail answers 'who did what in the account' (API activity). VPC Flow Logs record network traffic, and CloudWatch records performance metrics and application logs.

problem_ideas: An EC2 instance was terminated overnight and nobody admits doing it. Which service shows who did it?
An auditor needs 7 years of API activity. What must be configured beyond the default event history?
Sort each log need into CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs or CloudWatch: rejected SSH packets, a DeleteBucket call, high CPU.
Someone changed a security group from the CLI at 03:12. List the fields CloudTrail would show.
How many days of management events can you see for free without creating a trail?
A root user login happened from an unknown country. Which service recorded it?
